name: Peru Organic Decaf Sol y Cafe, Cajamarca
vendor_notes: Bright acidity, smooth body; citrus and floral to cocoa and caramel.
goal: Sweet, clean light-medium roast for espresso
rationale: Water-process decaf beans are already brownish, drier and more porous. They take up heat quickly, run through first crack at a slightly lower temperature, and crack quietly. Colour tells you little, so go by time and temperature. They also scorch and bake easily, so this plan uses the coolest charge (180 C) and gentler burner steps. Very light decaf tends to taste thin and sour as espresso, so drop ~9-10 C after FC (DTR ~18-19%) for caramel/cocoa sweetness while keeping the citrus. First crack temperature is the biggest unknown here: mark the first pops carefully.
steps: Preheat to 180 C, then hold steady 10+ min (BT/ET flat).
Charge 170 g at BT 180. Burner 65%, air 30, drum 90.
TP ~0:36 near 100 C. RoR is highest here, then falls.
At 166 C (~5:09): burner 42%. RoR ~10 and falling.
FC ~5:45 at ~172 C: burner 38%, air 55. Then 33%.
Drop ~7:10 at ~182 C (10 C after FC).

history.note: Initial plan from vendor data (Coffee Bean Corral) and Kaleido M1 behaviour. FC temperature is a guess until your first roast calibrates the probe.

Roast 1 (2026-09-29): 5-min preheat from cold at 100% burner, TP 0:37 and +16 C ahead by 2:00. FC came at 172 C (plan said 182): decaf cracks low on this probe. Dropped at 193 C, 21.7 C after FC (DTR 28%, a medium roast). v2: FC 172 at 5:45, drop 182 (+10 C), TP 0:42, steady preheat, charge burner 65%, earlier steps.

Re-fitted the first 3-4 minutes to five real roasts (2026-09-29 to 10-02): on this roaster TP comes at ~0:35 at 108-116 C (not ~0:42 at ~100 C), RoR is highest right after TP and only falls, dry end lands ~3:35-3:55 and FC ~7:12-7:25 at 187-189 C. Earlier versions put the start 10-20 C too low, which invited cutting heat early and a hot finish. FC temperature, roast level and development are unchanged.
